actions.label: Create Archive
actions.description: Packs files and folders into a ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ archive; output: path, files and size

source.description: File or folder to pack, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. out/*.csv

format.description: Format of the archive; auto: by the ending of target (.zip, .tar, .tar.gz or .tgz)

ifExists.description: If the archive exists: replace it once the new one is complete, or fail

outputs.name: output.path
outputs.description: Path of the archive

outputs.name: output.files
outputs.description: Number of entries packed: files and empty folders

outputs.name: output.size
outputs.description: Size of the archive in bytes

actions.errors: Fails when nothing matches the source, the format is not known from the ending, a file cannot be read, or the archive exists with ifExists: fail. The archive is written to a temporary file first, so a failure leaves an existing archive as it was. Links and special files are left out with a warning.

actions.label: Extract Archive
actions.description: Unpacks a ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ archive into a folder; output: the unpacked files

source.description: Archive to unpack, relative to the project folder or absolute

target.description: Folder to unpack into; it is created if missing

format.description: Format of the archive; auto: by the ending of source, else by its content

pattern.description: Only files whose name matches, e.g. *.csv; empty: all files

ifExists.description: If files exist in the folder: replace them, skip them, or fail before anything is written

maxSize.description: Largest total size of the unpacked files, e.g. 500MB or 10GB; protects against archives that unpack to far more than they hold

maxFiles.description: Largest number of entries in the archive

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the unpacked files

actions.errors: Fails before anything is written when an entry would leave the folder (.., absolute paths, drive letters, reserved names on Windows), the limits are exceeded or, with ifExists: fail (the default), a file exists. Also fails when the archive cannot be read or unpacks to more than maxSize while writing. Links and special files are left out with a warning.
limits: maxSize limits the total size of the unpacked files (default 1GB); it is counted again while writing, as an archive may state less than it holds.
maxFiles limits the number of entries in the archive (default 10,000).

actions.label: Abort
actions.description: Ends the workflow as failed

message.description: Reason for the run log; if empty, a default text names the action

actions.errors: Ends the workflow as failed at once, with the message: failure links are not followed and actions still running are cancelled.

actions.label: Check Condition
actions.description: Fails with a message when a condition is false

condition.description: Expression that must be true, e.g. {{ results.fetch.output.status == 200 }}

message.description: Message when the condition is false; empty: "the condition is false"
examples: No order files in the inbox

actions.example:
condition: "{{ len(results.list.output) > 0 }}"
message: No order files in the inbox

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: true if the condition is true

actions.errors: Fails with the message (or "the condition is false") when the condition is false, and when it is neither true nor false; the failure link can report it.

actions.label: Dummy
actions.description: Does nothing; collects branches into one point
actions.errors: Never fails.

actions.label: Log
actions.description: Writes a message to the run log

message.description: Text to write; may span several lines

actions.errors: Fails only for an invalid level.

actions.label: Run Pipeline
actions.description: Runs a pipeline with parameters; output: the counts of its transforms

pipeline.description: Pipeline file, relative to the project folder

params.description: Values for the parameters of the pipeline, by name

allowedTargets.description: Pipeline files this action may call, with wildcards and relative to the project folder, e.g. pipelines/import-*.pipeline.yaml; for a pipeline given by a variable or expression

rows.description: Records for core.from-result in the pipeline: a list, e.g. {{ results.files.output }}; items that are not objects become a record with the field value

outputs.name: output.transforms
outputs.description: Counts per transform id: read, written and errors

outputs.name: output.errors
outputs.description: Records that went to error links, in all transforms

outputs.name: output.rows
outputs.description: The records that reached core.to-result, each as an object

actions.errors: Fails when the pipeline stops with an error or cannot be started (file outside the project folder or missing, parameter not declared or invalid), when the pipeline is not in allowedTargets and when rows is not a list. Records on error links do not fail the action.
limits: output.rows holds at most maxRecords of core.to-result (default 100,000).

actions.label: Run Workflow
actions.description: Runs another workflow with parameters; output: its outputs

workflow.description: Workflow file, relative to the project folder

params.description: Values for the parameters of the workflow, by name

allowedTargets.description: Workflow files this action may call, with wildcards and relative to the project folder, e.g. workflows/import-*.workflow.yaml; for a workflow given by a variable or expression

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The outputs of the called workflow by name, e.g. output.ROWS

actions.errors: Fails when the workflow fails, cannot be started (file outside the project folder or missing, parameter not declared or invalid, calls itself) or is not in allowedTargets; cancelling the run cancels the called workflow.

actions.label: JavaScript
actions.description: Runs JavaScript with params; output: the value of return

script.description: JavaScript, the body of a function: params holds the values, return gives output; ${…} and {{ … }} in it are plain text

file.description: A .js file instead of script, relative to the project folder, e.g. scripts/total.js

params.description: Values for the script as params.NAME; may use ${…} and {{ … }}, a value of its own may be ${secret:…}

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The value of return, e.g. a number, text, list or object; null without return

actions.errors: Fails on a syntax error, an exception (with the line), a result that cannot be converted, a missing or too large script file, and when the timeout of the action or a cancelled run interrupts the script.
limits: The result may be at most 16 MiB as JSON and nested at most 100 levels; a script file or module may be at most 4 MiB.
The console keeps at most 1,000 lines per call, each cut at 8 KiB.
No access to files, network, processes or environment variables; require loads modules from scripts/ of the project only.

actions.label: Start
actions.description: Entry point of the workflow
actions.errors: Never fails.

actions.label: Success
actions.description: Ends the workflow successfully
actions.errors: Never fails. Ends the workflow as successful at once: its links are not followed and actions still running are cancelled.

actions.label: Wait
actions.description: Waits for a given time

duration.description: How long to wait, e.g. 30s, 5m or 1h30m

actions.errors: Fails for an empty or invalid duration; ends early, as failed, when the run is cancelled or the timeout of the action is reached.

actions.label: Execute SQL
actions.description: Runs an SQL statement on a database, e.g. to insert, update or delete rows

connection.description: Connection of the database (a file in connections/)

sql.description: The statement; values as @name with the value under params, never written into the statement

params.description: Values of the parameters @name of the statement; may use ${…} and {{ … }}

timeout.description: Longest time the statement may take

actions.example:
connection: app-db
sql: DELETE FROM orders WHERE created < @before
params:
  before: ${CUTOFF_DATE}

outputs.name: output.rowsAffected
outputs.description: Rows changed by the statement; -1 if the database does not tell

actions.errors: Fails when the connection cannot be opened, a parameter @name has no value, the database rejects the statement, or it takes longer than timeout.
limits: timeout limits the statement (default 5m).

actions.label: Query SQL
actions.description: Reads the rows of an SQL query into the workflow; output: rows, count, first and value

connection.description: Connection of the database (a file in connections/)

sql.description: The query; values as @name with the value under params, never written into the query

params.description: Values of the parameters @name of the query; may use ${…} and {{ … }}

maxRows.description: Most rows the query may return; more fail the action (for large results use a pipeline with db.table-input)

timeout.description: Longest time the query may take

actions.example:
connection: app-db
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS open FROM orders WHERE status = @status
params:
  status: open

outputs.name: output.rows
outputs.description: The rows, each an object with the columns by name

outputs.name: output.count
outputs.description: Number of rows

outputs.name: output.first
outputs.description: The first row; null without rows

outputs.name: output.value
outputs.description: The first column of the first row, e.g. of SELECT COUNT(*); null without rows

actions.errors: Fails when the connection cannot be opened, a parameter @name has no value, the database rejects the query, a column name appears twice, the query returns more than maxRows rows, or it takes longer than timeout.
limits: maxRows limits the rows (default 1000); they are held in memory and in the result of the run, so larger results belong into a pipeline with db.table-input.
timeout limits the query (default 1m).

actions.label: Copy Files
actions.description: Copies files or folders; output: the copied files

source.description: File or folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. *.csv

target.description: Target folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; for a single file also a new file name

ifExists.description: If a file exists in the target: replace it, skip it (it stays and is not in the output), or fail before anything is copied or moved

actions.example:
source: inbox/*.csv
target: archive/
ifExists: replace

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the copied files in the target, without skipped ones

actions.errors: Fails when nothing matches the source, and with ifExists: fail (the default) when a file exists in the target, checked before anything is copied; a file and a folder of the same name always conflict. A cancelled run stops between two blocks.

actions.label: Delete Files
actions.description: Deletes files or folders; output: the deleted paths

path.description: File or folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. *.tmp

recursive.description: Also delete folders with everything in them

ifMissing.description: If nothing matches the path: skip (nothing is deleted) or fail

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the deleted files and folders

actions.errors: Fails before deleting anything when a match is a folder and recursive is not set. Nothing to delete is no error, except with ifMissing: fail.

actions.label: File Exists
actions.description: Checks whether files or folders exist; output: the matching paths

path.description: File or folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. *.csv

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the matching files or folders, sorted

actions.errors: Fails when nothing of the kind matches the path, so that success and failure links can branch, and when the folder cannot be read.

actions.label: List Files
actions.description: Lists the files of a folder; output: path, name, size, modified and folder of each entry

folder.description: Folder to list, relative to the project folder or absolute

pattern.description: Names to include, with wildcards, e.g. *.csv

outputs.name: output[].path
outputs.description: Path of the entry; the list is sorted by path

outputs.name: output[].name
outputs.description: Name of the file or folder

outputs.name: output[].size
outputs.description: Size in bytes

outputs.name: output[].modified
outputs.description: Time of the last change, to the second

outputs.name: output[].folder
outputs.description: true for a folder

actions.errors: Fails when the folder does not exist or cannot be read; an empty folder gives an empty list.
limits: All entries are held in memory as the output; for very many files use the transform file.list.

actions.label: Create Folder
actions.description: Creates a folder with its parent folders; output: the path

path.description: Folder to create, relative to the project folder or absolute

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Path of the folder, relative paths with the project folder in front

actions.errors: Fails when a file of that name exists or the folder cannot be created; an existing folder is no error.

actions.label: Move Files
actions.description: Moves files or folders; output: the new paths

source.description: File or folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. *.csv

target.description: Target folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; for a single file also a new file name

ifExists.description: If a file exists in the target: replace it, skip it (it stays and is not in the output), or fail before anything is copied or moved

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: New paths of the moved files and folders, without skipped ones

actions.errors: Fails when nothing matches the source, and with ifExists: fail (the default) when a file exists in the target, checked before anything is moved; also when a copied source across drives cannot be deleted.

actions.label: Read File
actions.description: Reads a small text file into the workflow, as text, lines or JSON; output: content, value or lines, size and modified

path.description: File to read, relative to the project folder or absolute

format.description: How the content is read: text, lines (a list without line ends) or json (a value, e.g. {{ results.read.output.value.customers }})

encoding.description: Encoding of the file; auto recognizes UTF-8 with or without byte order mark and UTF-16

ifMissing.description: If the file does not exist: fail, or go on with empty content (output missing: true)

maxSize.description: Largest file to read, e.g. 500KB or 10MB; the content goes into the result of the run

outputs.name: output.content
outputs.description: The text of the file

outputs.name: output.lines
outputs.description: With format: lines, the lines without line ends

outputs.name: output.value
outputs.description: With format: json, the value

outputs.name: output.size
outputs.description: Size of the file in bytes

outputs.name: output.modified
outputs.description: Time of the last change; missing for a missing file

outputs.name: output.missing
outputs.description: true if the file does not exist (ifMissing: empty); else not set

actions.errors: Fails when the file is missing (unless ifMissing: empty), is a folder, is larger than maxSize, cannot be decoded or, with format: json, is not exactly one valid JSON value.
limits: maxSize limits the file (default 10MB); its content becomes part of the result of the run.

actions.label: Wait for File
actions.description: Waits until files exist; output: the matching paths

path.description: File to wait for, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. *.csv

interval.description: How often to look, e.g. 5s or 1m

maxWait.description: Give up and fail after this time; empty: wait until the action's timeout or the end of the run

stableFor.description: The size of the files must not change for this time, e.g. 10s; empty: do not check

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the matching files, sorted

actions.errors: Fails when no file matches after maxWait, or the files still change in size after maxWait (stableFor), and when the folder cannot be read.
limits: Looks every interval (default 5s, at least 10ms); without maxWait it waits until the timeout of the action or the end of the run.

actions.label: Write File
actions.description: Writes a text or a value as JSON to a file, replacing it or appending; output: path and size

path.description: File to write, relative to the project folder or absolute; missing folders are created

content.description: What to write: a text, or with format: json any value, e.g. {{ results.query.output.rows }}

format.description: text writes the content as text (other values as JSON), json writes the value as formatted JSON

encoding.description: Encoding of the file; utf-8-bom lets Excel and older Windows programs recognize umlauts

lineEnds.description: Line ends: as in the content, crlf (Windows) or lf

ifExists.description: If the file exists: replace it once the content is written, append to it, or fail

actions.example:
path: out/status.json
format: json
content: "{{ {'run': run.id, 'ok': true} }}"

outputs.name: output.path
outputs.description: Path of the file, relative paths with the project folder in front

outputs.name: output.size
outputs.description: Bytes written by this action (appended ones with ifExists: append)

actions.errors: Fails with ifExists: fail when the file exists, when the content cannot be written as JSON or in the encoding, and when the file cannot be written; replace writes a temporary file first, so a failure leaves the old file.

actions.label: HTTP Request
actions.description: Sends an HTTP request, e.g. to a REST API; output: status, headers and body of the answer

connection.description: Connection of the API (a file in connections/) with base address and sign-in; empty: url is a full address

url.description: Address with http:// or https://, e.g. https://api.example.com/orders; with connection relative to its baseUrl, e.g. orders

query.description: Query parameters, added to the address with encoding, e.g. status: open

headers.description: Headers of the request, e.g. Accept; tokens belong into a connection, never into the file

body.description: Body: a text is sent as text, other values (maps, lists, numbers) as JSON

timeout.description: Longest time for one request and its answer (with paginate: per page), e.g. 30s or 5m; the timeout of the action limits all together

failOnError.description: Fail the action if the answer has status 400 or above; false: the status is only in the output

maxSize.description: Largest answer to read, e.g. 10MB or 500KB; with paginate per page; with saveTo the largest file (default 1GB)

saveTo.description: Saves a successful answer (status 2xx) as a file instead of reading it, e.g. a ZIP or PDF; relative to the project folder or absolute. Written to a temporary file first, so no half file remains; output: path and size instead of body

ifExists.description: With saveTo, if the file exists: replace it once the download is complete, skip the request, or fail before the request

retryAfter.description: Asking again when the API answers 429 or 503 with Retry-After (wait in seconds or a date); on by default

maxRetries.description: Most repeats of one request after 429 or 503 with Retry-After; 0: none

maxWait.description: Longest wait the API may ask for; a longer one fails the action

paginate.description: Reading all pages of a paged API; output: items (all items), count and pages instead of body

style.description: How the next page is found: link (header Link rel=next), url (address in the body), cursor (value in the body as query parameter), page (page number) or offset (items read so far)

items.description: Path to the list of items in the body, e.g. data.items; empty: the body is the list

next.description: Path in the body to the address of the next page (url) or to the cursor (cursor), e.g. @odata.nextLink or meta.next_cursor

param.description: Query parameter for the cursor, page number or offset; empty: cursor, page or offset

start.description: First page number (page) or offset (offset); empty: 1 for page, 0 for offset

size.description: Items per page; a shorter page is the last one; with sizeParam it is also sent

sizeParam.description: Query parameter for the page size, e.g. per_page or limit

maxPages.description: Most pages to read; more fail the action

maxItems.description: Most items to read; more fail the action (use a pipeline for larger amounts)

actions.example:
connection: shop-api
url: orders
query:
  status: open

outputs.name: output.status
outputs.description: HTTP status of the answer (the last one with paginate)

outputs.name: output.headers
outputs.description: Headers of the answer with lowercase names; several values joined with a comma

outputs.name: output.body
outputs.description: The answer: a value for JSON, else text; not with paginate or a saved file

outputs.name: output.items
outputs.description: With paginate, the items of all pages

outputs.name: output.count
outputs.description: With paginate, the number of items

outputs.name: output.pages
outputs.description: With paginate, the number of pages read

outputs.name: output.path
outputs.description: With saveTo, the path of the saved file

outputs.name: output.size
outputs.description: With saveTo, the size of the saved file in bytes

outputs.name: output.skipped
outputs.description: With saveTo and ifExists: skip, true if the file existed and nothing was requested

actions.errors: Fails on status 400 and above (unless failOnError: false; the message shows the beginning of the answer), when there is no answer within timeout, the answer is larger than maxSize, the API asks to wait longer than retryAfter.maxWait, or paginate exceeds its limits or leads to another host. With saveTo and ifExists: fail, fails before the request when the file exists; a failed download leaves no file.
limits: timeout limits each request (default 60s; with paginate per page); the timeout of the action limits all together.
maxSize limits the answer (default 10MB, per page with paginate) or with saveTo the file (default 1GB).
After 429 or 503 with Retry-After, the request is repeated at most retryAfter.maxRetries times (default 3), waiting at most retryAfter.maxWait (default 1m).
paginate reads at most maxPages pages (default 100) and maxItems items (default 10,000), all on the host of the first page.

actions.label: HTTP Response
actions.description: Answers the caller of an HTTP trigger with status, headers and body; output: sent and status

headers.description: Headers of the answer, e.g. Content-Type

body.description: Body: a text is sent as text, other values (maps, lists, numbers) as JSON

actions.example:
status: 404
body:
  error: "customer {{ params.KDNR }} not found"

outputs.name: output.sent
outputs.description: true if this was the answer to the caller

outputs.name: output.status
outputs.description: The status of the answer

actions.errors: Fails only for a status that is not a number from 200 to 599. Without a waiting caller, or when the caller has been answered already, it sends nothing (sent: false) and the workflow goes on.
limits: The caller waits only for the response timeout of the trigger; later answers are not sent.

actions.label: Send Mail
actions.description: Sends a mail through a mail server, with text or HTML and attachments

connection.description: Connection of the mail server (a file in connections/)

from.description: Sender, e.g. Runnel <runnel@example.com>; empty: from of the connection

to.description: Recipients, separated by commas, e.g. ops@example.com, Ada <ada@example.com>

cc.description: Recipients of a copy, separated by commas

bcc.description: Recipients of a blind copy, separated by commas; they do not appear in the mail

replyTo.description: Address for replies, if not the sender

html.description: Text of the mail as HTML; with body, mail programs show the HTML and keep the text as an alternative

attachments.description: Files to attach, relative to the project folder; at most 25 MB together

actions.example:
connection: mail
to: ${ADMIN_MAIL}
subject: "Import failed: {{ run.id }}"
body: "{{ run.lastError }}"

outputs.name: output.messageId
outputs.description: Message-ID of the mail

outputs.name: output.recipients
outputs.description: Number of recipients in to, cc and bcc

outputs.name: output.size
outputs.description: Size of the mail in bytes

actions.errors: Fails when the mail has no sender or recipient, an address or attachment is invalid, the attachments are too large, the server cannot be reached within the timeout of the connection, refuses the sign-in or a recipient, or accepts no mail of this size.
limits: Attachments may be at most 25 MB together.
The timeout of the connection limits connecting and sending (default 1m).

actions.label: PowerShell
actions.description: Runs a PowerShell script with named parameters; output: exitCode, stdout, stderr and optionally JSON

script.description: The script; no ${…} or {{ … }} – values come as params

file.description: A script file instead of script, relative to the project folder, e.g. scripts/cleanup.ps1

params.description: Named parameters of the script (param(...)); numbers, true/false, lists and objects keep their type; may use ${…} and {{ … }}

json.description: Read the last JSON value of stdout (e.g. of ConvertTo-Json) into output.json

edition.description: auto: PowerShell 7 (pwsh) if installed, else Windows PowerShell 5.1; pwsh or windows to choose one

workdir.description: Working folder, relative to the project folder; empty: the project folder

env.description: Further environment variables, e.g. secrets ($env:NAME in the script)

maxOutput.description: Largest size of stdout and of stderr kept, e.g. 500KB or 10MB; more is dropped (truncated)

timeout.description: Longest time the script may run; then it ends with all processes it started

actions.example:
script: |
  param([string]$Folder)
  Get-ChildItem $Folder | Select-Object Name, Length | ConvertTo-Json
params:
  Folder: data
json: true

outputs.name: output.exitCode
outputs.description: Exit code of PowerShell

outputs.name: output.stdout
outputs.description: Standard output; values of env are hidden

outputs.name: output.stderr
outputs.description: Error output; values of env are hidden

outputs.name: output.truncated
outputs.description: true if stdout or stderr was longer than maxOutput

outputs.name: output.duration
outputs.description: Running time, e.g. 1.25s

outputs.name: output.json
outputs.description: With json, the last JSON value of stdout, e.g. of ConvertTo-Json

actions.errors: Fails when the edition is not installed, the script file is missing, the script ends with an exit code other than 0 (an uncaught error included), it runs longer than timeout (it is ended with all processes it started), or with json stdout holds no JSON.
limits: timeout limits the script (default 10m).
maxOutput limits stdout and stderr each (default 1MB, at most 1GB); more is dropped.

actions.label: Run Program
actions.description: Starts a program with arguments, without a shell; output: exitCode, stdout and stderr

program.description: Program to start: a name found through PATH, or a path relative to the project folder; may use variables of the project, but no parameters of the workflow and no expressions

args.description: Arguments, one per entry; each is passed as one argument, never read by a shell, and may use ${…} and {{ … }}

okCodes.description: Exit codes that count as success; empty: 0 only

workdir.description: Working folder, relative to the project folder; empty: the project folder

env.description: Further environment variables; the only place for secrets (${secret:…}), as arguments are visible to other users

input.description: Text for stdin; missing: stdin is empty, so that a program waiting for input does not hang

encoding.description: Encoding of stdout and stderr; auto: UTF-8, else the OEM code page of Windows

json.description: Read the last JSON value of stdout into output.json

maxOutput.description: Largest size of stdout and of stderr kept, e.g. 500KB or 10MB; more is dropped (truncated)

timeout.description: Longest time the program may run; then it ends with all processes it started

actions.example:
program: robocopy
args: [ data/out, "\\\\server\\share\\in", "*.csv", /MIR ]
okCodes: [ 0, 1, 2, 3 ]
timeout: 10m

outputs.name: output.exitCode
outputs.description: Exit code of the program

outputs.name: output.stdout
outputs.description: Standard output, decoded; values of env are hidden

outputs.name: output.stderr
outputs.description: Error output, decoded; values of env are hidden

outputs.name: output.truncated
outputs.description: true if stdout or stderr was longer than maxOutput

outputs.name: output.duration
outputs.description: Running time, e.g. 1.25s

outputs.name: output.json
outputs.description: With json, the last JSON value of stdout

actions.errors: Fails when the program is not found, its exit code is not in okCodes (default 0; the message shows the last lines of stderr), it runs longer than timeout (it is ended with all processes it started), or with json stdout holds no JSON. Arguments of .bat and .cmd files with characters that cmd.exe interprets are refused.
limits: timeout limits the program (default 10m).
maxOutput limits stdout and stderr each (default 1MB, at most 1GB); more is dropped.

actions.label: Delete Files on Server
actions.description: Deletes files or folders on a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the deleted paths

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

path.description: File or folder on the server, e.g. /outgoing/*.csv (relative: to the folder after the sign-in); wildcards are allowed in the name and match case-sensitively

recursive.description: Also delete folders with everything in them

ifMissing.description: If nothing matches the path: skip (nothing is deleted) or fail

timeout.description: Longest time for each matching file or folder with its content, e.g. 5m; the timeout of the action limits all together

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the deleted files and folders on the server

actions.errors: Fails before deleting anything when a match is a folder and recursive is not set, and when the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout). Nothing to delete is no error, except with ifMissing: fail.
limits: A path with wildcards may match at most 10,000 entries.
timeout limits each match with its content (default 10m).

actions.label: Download Files
actions.description: Downloads files or folders from a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the downloaded files

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

source.description: File or folder on the server, e.g. /outgoing/*.csv (relative: to the folder after the sign-in); wildcards are allowed in the name and match case-sensitively

target.description: Local folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; for a single file also a new file name

ifExists.description: If a local file exists: replace it, skip it (it stays and is not in the output), or fail before anything is downloaded

maxSize.description: Largest file to download, e.g. 500MB; a larger one fails the action; empty: no limit

timeout.description: Longest time for one file, e.g. 30m; the timeout of the action limits all together

actions.example:
connection: partner-sftp
source: /outgoing/*.csv
target: inbox/
ifExists: replace

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Local paths of the downloaded files, without skipped ones

actions.errors: Fails when nothing matches the source, the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout), a file is larger than maxSize, a name from the server is no safe local name, and with ifExists: fail (the default) when a local file exists, checked before anything is downloaded. A failed download leaves no half file.
limits: timeout limits each file (default 10m); the timeout of the action limits all together.
maxSize limits each file; empty: no limit.

actions.label: File Exists on Server
actions.description: Checks whether files or folders exist on a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the matching paths

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

path.description: File or folder on the server, e.g. /outgoing/*.csv (relative: to the folder after the sign-in); wildcards are allowed in the name and match case-sensitively

timeout.description: Longest time for the check, e.g. 1m; the timeout of the action limits all together

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the matching files or folders on the server

actions.errors: Fails when nothing of the kind matches the path, so that success and failure links can branch, and when the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout).
limits: A path with wildcards may match at most 10,000 entries.
timeout limits the check (default 10m).

actions.label: List Files on Server
actions.description: Lists the files of a folder on a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: path, name, size, modified and folder of each entry

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

folder.description: Folder on the server, e.g. /outgoing (relative: to the folder after the sign-in, . is that folder)

pattern.description: Names to include, with wildcards that match case-sensitively, e.g. *.csv

timeout.description: Longest time for the listing, e.g. 1m; the timeout of the action limits all together

outputs.name: output[].path
outputs.description: Path of the entry on the server; the list is sorted by path

outputs.name: output[].name
outputs.description: Name of the file or folder

outputs.name: output[].size
outputs.description: Size in bytes

outputs.name: output[].modified
outputs.description: Time of the last change, to the second

outputs.name: output[].folder
outputs.description: true for a folder

actions.errors: Fails when the folder does not exist on the server, the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout), or there are more entries than the limit.
limits: At most 10,000 entries, as they are held in the result of the run; narrow the list with pattern or without recursive.
timeout limits the listing (default 10m).

actions.label: Create Folder on Server
actions.description: Creates a folder with its parent folders on a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the path

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

path.description: Folder to create on the server, e.g. /outgoing/archive (relative: to the folder after the sign-in)

timeout.description: Longest time to create the folder, e.g. 1m; the timeout of the action limits all together

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Path of the folder on the server

actions.errors: Fails when a file of that name exists, the folder cannot be created, or the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout); an existing folder is no error.
limits: timeout limits creating the folder (default 10m).

actions.label: Move Files on Server
actions.description: Moves or renames files or folders on a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the new paths

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

source.description: File or folder on the server, e.g. /outgoing/*.csv (relative: to the folder after the sign-in); wildcards are allowed in the name and match case-sensitively

target.description: Folder on the same server, e.g. /outgoing/archive/; for a single file or folder also a new name

ifExists.description: If a file exists in the target: replace it, skip it (the source stays and is not in the output), or fail before anything is moved

timeout.description: Longest time for each file or folder, e.g. 1m; the timeout of the action limits all together

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: New paths on the server, without skipped ones

actions.errors: Fails when nothing matches the source, the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout), the server cannot rename (e.g. to another file system), and with ifExists: fail (the default) when a file exists in the target, checked before anything is moved.
limits: A path with wildcards may match at most 10,000 entries.
timeout limits each file or folder (default 10m).

actions.label: Upload Files
actions.description: Uploads files or folders to a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the uploaded files

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

source.description: Local file or folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; wildcards are allowed in the name, e.g. *.csv

target.description: Folder on the server, e.g. /incoming/ (relative: to the folder after the sign-in); for a single file also a new file name

ifExists.description: If a file exists on the server: replace it, skip it (it stays and is not in the output), or fail before anything is uploaded

timeout.description: Longest time for one file, e.g. 30m; the timeout of the action limits all together

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the uploaded files on the server, without skipped ones

actions.errors: Fails when nothing matches the source, the connection fails (host key, certificate or sign-in refused, no answer within timeout), and with ifExists: fail (the default) when a file exists on the server, checked before anything is uploaded. Each file is written to a temporary name and renamed when complete.
limits: timeout limits each file (default 10m); the timeout of the action limits all together.

actions.label: Wait for File on Server
actions.description: Waits until files exist on a server (SFTP, FTPS or FTP); output: the matching paths

connection.description: Connection of the server (a file in connections/)

path.description: File to wait for on the server, e.g. /outgoing/*.csv (relative: to the folder after the sign-in); wildcards are allowed in the name and match case-sensitively

interval.description: How often to look, e.g. 5s or 1m

maxWait.description: Give up and fail after this time; empty: wait until the action's timeout or the end of the run

stableFor.description: The size of the files must not change for this time, e.g. 30s; empty: do not check

timeout.description: Longest time for one look on the server, e.g. 30s; after it Runnel connects again

actions.example:
connection: partner-sftp
path: /outgoing/*.csv
interval: 1m
maxWait: 2h
stableFor: 30s

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Paths of the matching files on the server, sorted

actions.errors: Fails when no file matches after maxWait, or the files still change in size after maxWait (stableFor), and when the first connection fails or a host key, certificate or sign-in is refused. A dropped connection or a look longer than timeout is retried at the next look.
limits: Looks every interval (default 5s, at least 10ms); without maxWait it waits until the timeout of the action or the end of the run.
timeout limits each look (default 1m).
A path with wildcards may match at most 10,000 entries.

transforms.label: Calculate
transforms.description: Sets fields for every record: a copy of another field, a fixed value, a default or a calculated value

fields.description: Fields to calculate, in this order: a later field can use an earlier one

name.description: Name of the field; an existing field of the same name gets the new value

value.description: Value of the field: an expression in {{ … }} evaluated for every record, e.g. {{ record.price * record.quantity }}; text around {{ … }} makes the result a text; without {{ … }} a fixed value (a number, true, false or a text)

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The result, with the type of the expression; text around {{ … }} gives text

transforms.records: Passes every record on with the fields set, in their order.
transforms.errors: A record for which an expression cannot be evaluated goes unchanged to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops.

transforms.label: Add Constants
transforms.description: Adds fields with the same value to every record

fields.description: Fields to add; an existing field of the same name gets the value

value.description: Value of the field: text, number, true/false, or an expression evaluated once per run, e.g. {{ now() }}

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The value, with its type; an existing field keeps its position

transforms.records: Passes every record on with the fields set.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when it starts if a value cannot be evaluated; never for a single record.

transforms.label: Convert Types
transforms.description: Converts fields to another type, with a number or date format

format.description: Number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy, to read text or to write text; empty: 1234.5 and ISO dates

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The value converted to the type of the field

transforms.records: Passes every record on with the fields converted; a field missing in a record stays missing.
transforms.errors: A record with a value that cannot be converted goes unchanged to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops with record and field. Numbers are not rounded: 1.5 is no int.

transforms.label: Remove Duplicates
transforms.description: Passes on the first record of each combination of values and drops repeated ones

fields.description: Fields whose values together make a record a duplicate of an earlier one; empty: all fields

ignoreCase.description: Compare text regardless of upper and lower case

transforms.example:
fields: [email]
ignoreCase: true
transforms.records: Passes on the first record of each combination of values at once and drops the repeated ones; the log counts them.
transforms.errors: Never fails while the pipeline runs.
limits: Holds the combinations seen in memory; it grows with the number of different records.

transforms.label: Dummy
transforms.description: Passes all records on unchanged
transforms.records: Passes all records on unchanged to all data links.
transforms.errors: Never fails.

transforms.label: Filter
transforms.description: Passes on the records for which a condition is true

condition.description: Expression that must be true for a record to pass, e.g. {{ record.amount > 0 }}; a comparison with an empty value is false

else.description: Transform for the records for which the condition is false; a data link must lead there, and the records that pass go to the other data links. Empty: they are dropped

transforms.example:
condition: "{{ record.umsatz > 0 && record.ort != '' }}"
else: rejected
transforms.records: Passes the records for which the condition is true to the data links; the others go to the transform named in else, or are dropped and counted in the log.
transforms.errors: A record whose condition cannot be evaluated goes to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops.

transforms.label: Records from Workflow
transforms.description: Passes on the records the calling workflow gave to the pipeline (rows)
transforms.records: Passes on the records given to the run (rows of core.run-pipeline, the JSON list of a request to an http trigger), their fields in the order of their names; none when the pipeline is started on its own.
transforms.errors: Never fails while the pipeline runs.

transforms.label: Generate Rows
transforms.description: Creates records with constant fields

rows.description: Number of records to create, e.g. 1000 or ${ROWS}

fields.description: Fields of every record, with a constant value

rowNumberField.description: Name of a field for the number of the record, starting at 1; empty: none

transforms.example:
rows: 10
rowNumberField: n
fields:
  - { name: status, value: new }

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The constant value, with the type of the value

outputs.name: <rowNumberField>
outputs.description: Number of the record, starting at 1

transforms.records: Creates rows records with the same fields and passes them to all data links; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when rows is not a whole number of 0 or more.

transforms.label: Group By
transforms.description: Combines records with the same values into one, with count, sum and other aggregates

groupBy.description: Fields whose values form a group; empty: one record for all

aggregates.description: Fields computed per group, after the group fields

function.description: count: records (or values of field), countDistinct: different values, sum, avg, min, max, first, last, concat: values as text

field.description: Field the function is applied to; empty for count: all records

separator.description: Text between the values of concat; empty: comma and space

outputs.name: <groupBy>
outputs.description: The values of the group, with their type

outputs.name: <aggregates[].name>
outputs.description: The aggregate: int for count and countDistinct, text for concat, decimal for avg of int, else the type of the field

transforms.records: Passes on one record per group, with only the group fields and the aggregates, in the order the groups first appeared, once its input has ended; without groupBy exactly one record, also for no input.
transforms.errors: A record with a value that does not fit its function (e.g. text in sum) goes to the error link and counts in no group; without one, the pipeline stops.
limits: Holds one entry per group in memory; it grows with the number of groups, not of records.

transforms.label: Log
transforms.description: Writes records to the run log and passes them on

every.description: Writes every n-th record, e.g. 1000 for large data

fields.description: Fields to write, in this order; empty: all fields

transforms.example: fields: [kdnr, name]
transforms.records: Passes all records on unchanged to all data links; writes every n-th of them (every) to the run log.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline only for an invalid level.

transforms.label: Map Values
transforms.description: Replaces the values of a field by a table, e.g. codes by names

as.description: Field for the result; empty: the field itself

values.description: The table: a value and what it becomes

from.description: Value to replace, compared as text; empty: an empty value

to.description: What it becomes: text, number or true/false; missing: an empty value

default.description: Result for values that are not in the table, also for empty ones; missing: the value stays as it is

ignoreCase.description: Compare text regardless of upper and lower case

outputs.name: <as>
outputs.description: The new value; without as, it replaces the value of field

transforms.records: Passes every record on with the value replaced by the table, the default, or unchanged.
transforms.errors: Never fails while the pipeline runs.

transforms.label: Merge Join
transforms.description: Joins the records of two inputs sorted by the same keys, like a join in a database

left.description: Transform whose data link brings the left records

right.description: Transform whose data link brings the right records

keys.description: Fields that must be equal; both inputs must be sorted by them in ascending order, e.g. with core.sort

right.description: Field of the right records; empty: the same name

join.description: inner: only records with a partner; left: also left records without one; full: also right records without one

transforms.example:
left: orders
right: customers
keys:
  - { left: customerId, right: id }
join: left
transforms.records: Passes on one record per pair of left and right records with the same keys (n × m for repeated keys): the left fields, then the right fields the left records do not have. With join: left also left records without a partner, with full also right ones; their missing fields are empty.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when an input is not sorted by the keys in ascending order, or when keys cannot be compared (e.g. text with a number).
limits: Holds only the records of one key of each input in memory, so the inputs may be of any size.

transforms.label: Script
transforms.description: Runs JavaScript for every record: return a new record, several or none

script.description: JavaScript run for every record, the body of a function: record holds its fields, params the values; return an object (the new record), a list of objects (several records) or null (none); ${…} and {{ … }} in it are plain text

file.description: A .js file instead of script, relative to the project folder, e.g. scripts/clean.js

init.description: JavaScript run once before the first record, e.g. let count = 0; its variables and functions are seen by script and end

end.description: JavaScript run once after the last record, the body of a function: return an object or a list of objects for further records, e.g. a total

params.description: Values for the script as params.NAME; may use ${…}, a value of its own may be ${secret:…}

fields.description: Fields of the returned records with their type, in this order: each value is converted to the type, other properties are dropped; without fields the types follow the values

type.description: Type of the field; a returned value is converted to it

maxRecordTime.description: Longest time the script may take for one record; a record that takes longer goes to the error link

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: A declared field, converted to its type; without fields the types follow the values

transforms.records: Passes on what the script returns for each record: an object as one record, a list as several, null as none; end may return further records after the last one.
transforms.errors: A record whose script throws an exception, returns a value that cannot be converted or takes longer than maxRecordTime goes to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops. A syntax error, a missing script file and errors in init or end stop the pipeline.
limits: maxRecordTime limits the time per record (default 1s); init and end have no limit of their own.
The console keeps at most 1,000 lines per copy, each cut at 8 KiB; a script file or module may be at most 4 MiB.
No access to files, network, processes or environment variables; require loads modules from scripts/ of the project only.

transforms.label: Select Fields
transforms.description: Keeps, orders and renames fields, or removes fields

fields.description: Fields to keep, in this order, optionally renamed; all others are removed

name.description: Name of the field in the incoming records

as.description: New name of the field; empty: the name stays

remove.description: Fields to remove; all others are kept. Use either fields or remove

outputs.name: <fields[].as>
outputs.description: A kept field under its new name

transforms.records: Passes every record on with only the fields listed in fields (in this order; a missing one is empty), or without the fields listed in remove.
transforms.errors: Never fails while the pipeline runs.

transforms.label: Sequence
transforms.description: Numbers the records in the order they arrive, also per group

name.description: Name of the field for the number; an existing field of the same name gets the number

start.description: Number of the first record, e.g. 1 or ${START}

step.description: Difference between two numbers, e.g. 10 for 10, 20, 30; may be negative

groupBy.description: Fields whose values form a group that counts on its own from start; empty: one count for all records

transforms.example:
name: position
start: 10
step: 10
groupBy: [Nr]

outputs.name: <name>
outputs.description: The number of the record, from start in steps of step

transforms.records: Passes every record on with the number, in the order they arrive.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when start or step is not a whole number.
limits: With groupBy, one counter per group is kept in memory.

transforms.label: Sort
transforms.description: Sorts the records by fields; keeps all records in memory

fields.description: Fields to sort by, the first one first

ignoreCase.description: Compare text regardless of upper and lower case

transforms.records: Passes all records on, sorted and stable, once its input has ended; empty values come last.
transforms.errors: A record whose value cannot be sorted together with the values before (another kind, e.g. text among numbers) goes to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops.
limits: Holds all records in memory until its input has ended.

transforms.label: Split Field
transforms.description: Splits the text of a field into several fields or into one record per part

separator.description: Text between the parts, e.g. ; or , (with the space)

into.description: Fields for the parts, in order; more parts than fields stay together in the last one, missing parts are empty. Not with rows

rows.description: One record per part instead: the field holds the part, the other fields are copied

indexField.description: With rows: field for the position of the part, starting at 1

keepEmpty.description: With rows: also a record for empty parts (a;;b); a record whose field is empty is always passed on once

transforms.example:
field: name
separator: ", "
into: [lastName, firstName]

outputs.name: <into>
outputs.description: The parts in order; more parts stay together in the last field, missing ones are empty

outputs.name: <indexField>
outputs.description: With rows, the position of the part, starting at 1

transforms.records: With into, passes every record on with the parts; with rows, one record per part with field set to the part, and a record without a value once.
transforms.errors: Never fails while the pipeline runs.

transforms.label: Stream Lookup
transforms.description: Adds the fields of the matching lookup record to each record; the lookup data comes over an info link

keys.description: Fields of the record and the fields of the lookup data they must be equal to, compared as text

lookupField.description: Field of the lookup data; empty: the same name

return.description: Fields of the matching lookup record added to the record

as.description: Field for the value; empty: the name of the lookup field

default.description: Value when no lookup record matches; missing: an empty value

notFound.description: Records without a matching lookup record: keep them with the defaults, drop them, or treat them as errors (error link)

multiple.description: Several matching lookup records: take the first in the order they arrived, or treat the record as an error

maxRecords.description: Most records of the lookup data held in memory; more stop the pipeline (for larger tables use db.lookup)

outputs.name: <return[].as>
outputs.description: The value of the lookup field, or its default; without as, under the name of the lookup field

transforms.records: Reads the info link to the end first, then passes every record of the data links on with the returned fields; with notFound: drop, records without a match are dropped.
transforms.errors: With notFound: error or multiple: error, such a record goes to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops. More lookup records than maxRecords and a missing info link stop the pipeline.
limits: maxRecords limits the lookup records held in memory (default 100,000).

transforms.label: Switch
transforms.description: Passes each record to the link of the first case whose condition is true

cases.description: Conditions in order; the first one that is true decides

when.description: Condition, e.g. {{ record.country == 'DE' }}; a comparison with an empty value is false

to.description: Id of the transform the record goes to; a data link must lead there

default.description: Transform for records that match no case; empty: they are dropped

transforms.records: Passes each record to the transform of the first case whose condition is true, else to default; without default, the others are dropped and counted in the log.
transforms.errors: A record whose condition cannot be evaluated goes to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops.

transforms.label: Records to Workflow
transforms.description: Returns the records to the calling workflow (output.rows) and passes them on

maxRecords.description: Most records to return; more stop the pipeline, as they are held in memory

transforms.example: maxRecords: 1000
transforms.records: Passes all records on unchanged and adds them to the result of the pipeline: core.run-pipeline returns them as output.rows.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when there are more records than maxRecords, or maxRecords is not a whole number of 1 or more.
limits: maxRecords limits the records held in memory for the result (default 100,000).

transforms.label: CSV Input
transforms.description: Reads the rows of a CSV file as records

path.description: CSV file to read, relative to the project folder or absolute

delimiter.description: Character between the values, e.g. ; or \t for tab; empty: comma

header.description: Whether the first row holds the names of the columns

encoding.description: Encoding of the file; auto recognizes UTF-8 and UTF-16 by their byte order mark and reads UTF-8 otherwise

fields.description: Columns to read, with type and format, matched by name (or from) in the header or else by position; empty: all columns as text

from.description: Column in the header; empty: the column named like the field

type.description: Type of the value; empty: text

format.description: Number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy; empty: 1234.5 and ISO dates

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The column with the type of the field; without fields, every column as text, named by the header or field1, field2 …

transforms.records: Creates one record per row (without the header) and passes it to all data links; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: A row with another number of values than the first, or with a value that does not fit its type, goes with its values as text to the error link, the message with file, line and column; without one, the pipeline stops. A missing file, a column missing in the header and other errors in the CSV (e.g. a stray quote) stop the pipeline.
limits: The file is read as a stream, so it may be larger than the memory.

transforms.label: CSV Output
transforms.description: Writes records to a CSV file and passes them on

path.description: CSV file to write, relative to the project folder or absolute

delimiter.description: Character between the values, e.g. ; or \t for tab; empty: comma

header.description: Whether the first row holds the names of the columns

encoding.description: Encoding of the file; utf-8-bom lets Excel recognize umlauts, utf-16 is little endian with byte order mark

ifExists.description: If the file exists: replace it once all records are written, append to it, or fail

fields.description: Columns to write, in this order, with a format; empty: all fields of the records

name.description: Name of the field to write

as.description: Name of the column in the header; empty: the name of the field

format.description: Number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy; empty: 1234.5 and ISO dates

transforms.records: Passes every written record on unchanged to all data links.
transforms.errors: A record with a value that cannot be written in its format or encoding goes to the error link and is not written; without one, the pipeline stops. With ifExists: fail, an existing file stops the pipeline before anything is written. Except with ifExists: append, the file is written to a temporary file first and replaces an existing one only once all records are written, so a failure leaves the old file.

transforms.label: Database Lookup
transforms.description: Adds the columns of the matching row of a database table to each record

connection.description: Connection of the database (a file in connections/)

table.description: Table to look in: table or schema.table

keys.description: Fields of the record and the columns they must be equal to

column.description: Column of the table; empty: the name of the field

return.description: Columns of the matching row added to the record

as.description: Field for the value; empty: the name of the column

default.description: Value when no row matches; missing: an empty value

notFound.description: Records without a matching row: keep them with the defaults, drop them, or treat them as errors (error link)

multiple.description: Several matching rows: take the first the database returns, or treat the record as an error

cache.description: Results kept in memory, by key; 0: ask the database for every record

timeout.description: Longest time one query may take

outputs.name: <return[].as>
outputs.description: The value of the column, or its default; without as, under the name of the column

transforms.records: Passes every record on with the returned columns; with notFound: drop, records without a matching row are dropped.
transforms.errors: With notFound: error or multiple: error, such a record goes to the error link; without one, the pipeline stops. A failing query or one longer than timeout stops the pipeline.
limits: cache keeps the results of the last keys in memory (default 1000); timeout limits each query (default 30s).

transforms.label: Table Input
transforms.description: Reads the rows of an SQL query as records, one field per column

connection.description: Connection of the database (a file in connections/)

sql.description: The query; values as @name with the value under params, never written into the query

params.description: Values of the parameters @name of the query; may use ${…}

timeout.description: Longest time the query may take, reading all rows included

transforms.example:
connection: app-db
sql: SELECT id, name, amount FROM orders WHERE status = @status
params:
  status: open
transforms.records: Creates one record per row of the query, one field per column in their order with the type the database returns, and passes it to all data links; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when the connection cannot be opened, a parameter @name has no value, the database rejects the query, a column name appears twice, or reading all rows takes longer than timeout.
limits: timeout limits the query with reading all rows (default 5m); the rows are read as a stream.

transforms.label: Table Output
transforms.description: Inserts each record as a new row into a database table

connection.description: Connection of the database (a file in connections/)

table.description: Table to write to, e.g. orders or sales.orders

fields.description: Fields to write, each into the column of the same name; empty: all fields (not those starting with _)

timeout.description: Longest time one transaction may take

transforms.example:
connection: app-db
table: orders
fields: [id, customer, amount]
commitSize: 1000
transforms.records: Passes every written record on unchanged to all data links, once its transaction is committed.
transforms.errors: When a transaction fails, its rows are written again one by one with an error link, so that only the failing records go there; without one, the pipeline stops and the transactions committed before stay.
limits: commitSize rows per transaction (default 1000); timeout limits each transaction (default 5m).

transforms.label: Insert or Update
transforms.description: Updates the row with the same keys in a database table, or inserts the record as a new row

connection.description: Connection of the database (a file in connections/)

table.description: Table to write to, e.g. orders or sales.orders

fields.description: Fields to write, each into the column of the same name; empty: all fields (not those starting with _)

timeout.description: Longest time one transaction may take

keys.description: Fields that identify a row; SQLite and PostgreSQL need a unique index on them

update.description: Fields to change in an existing row; empty: all written fields except the keys

transforms.example:
connection: app-db
table: customers
keys: [id]
fields: [id, name, email]
transforms.records: Passes every written record on unchanged to all data links, once its transaction is committed.
transforms.errors: When a transaction fails, its rows are written again one by one with an error link, so that only the failing records go there; without one, the pipeline stops and the transactions committed before stay.
limits: commitSize rows per transaction (default 1000); timeout limits each transaction (default 5m).

transforms.label: Excel Input
transforms.description: Reads the rows of a sheet of an Excel workbook (.xlsx) as records

path.description: Workbook to read (.xlsx or .xlsm), relative to the project folder or absolute

sheet.description: Sheet to read: its name, or its number like 2; empty: the first sheet

range.description: Where the table is: its first cell like A3, with last column A3:F or with last row B2:D100; empty: from the first row with values

header.description: Whether the first row of the table holds the names of the columns

emptyRows.description: Empty rows in the table: skip them, or stop at the first one, e.g. when notes follow the table

fields.description: Columns to read, with type and format, matched by name (or from) in the header or else by position; empty: all columns with the values of their cells

from.description: Column in the header; empty: the column named like the field

type.description: Type of the value; empty: as in the cell (text, number, true/false, date)

format.description: For text in the cells: number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy; numbers and dates of Excel need none

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The cell with the type of the field; without fields, every column with the type of its cells (text, int, decimal, bool, date, datetime)

transforms.records: Creates one record per row of the table and passes it to all data links; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: A row with an error value like #N/A in a cell, or a value that does not fit its type, goes to the error link with the cell in the message; without one, the pipeline stops. A missing sheet or column, .xls, .xlsb and workbooks with a password stop the pipeline.
limits: The sheet is read as a stream; its XML may unpack to at most 4 GB, the shared texts to 256 MB.

transforms.label: Excel Output
transforms.description: Writes records to a sheet of an Excel workbook (.xlsx) and passes them on

path.description: Workbook to write (.xlsx or .xlsm), relative to the project folder or absolute

sheet.description: Name of the sheet; empty: Sheet1

header.description: Whether the first row holds the names of the columns, bold and frozen

ifExists.description: If the workbook exists: replace it once all records are written, fail, or replace only the sheet (sheet) and keep the other sheets, charts and formulas

fields.description: Columns to write, in this order, with a number format; empty: all fields of the records

name.description: Name of the field to write

as.description: Name of the column in the header; empty: the name of the field

format.description: Number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm, as in the other outputs; Excel shows separators and names in the language of the user; empty: numbers as General, dates as short date

excelFormat.description: Number format of Excel as in English Excel instead of format, e.g. 0.0%, 0.0 "kg" or [Red]-#,##0.00

transforms.records: Passes every written record on unchanged to all data links.
transforms.errors: A record with a value Excel cannot hold (more than 32,767 characters in a cell, a date before 1900, NaN) goes to the error link and is not written; without one, the pipeline stops. More than 1,048,576 rows, more than 16,384 columns and an existing workbook with ifExists: fail stop the pipeline. With replace, the workbook is written to a temporary file first.
limits: The rows go through temporary files; the finished workbook is packed in memory at the end.

transforms.label: List Files
transforms.description: Reads the files of a folder as records: path, name, extension, size, modified and folder

folder.description: Folder to list, relative to the project folder or absolute

pattern.description: Names to include, with wildcards, e.g. *.csv

transforms.example:
folder: inbox
pattern: "*.csv"
recursive: true

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: Path of the entry

outputs.name: name
outputs.description: Name of the file or folder

outputs.name: extension
outputs.description: Ending of the name with the dot, e.g. .csv; empty for folders

outputs.name: size
outputs.description: Size in bytes

outputs.name: modified
outputs.description: Time of the last change, to the second

outputs.name: folder
outputs.description: true for a folder

transforms.records: Creates one record per entry of the folder, in the order of their paths; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when the folder does not exist or cannot be read.

transforms.label: HTTP Response
transforms.description: Answers the caller of an HTTP trigger with the records as JSON and passes them on

single.description: Answer with the first record as an object instead of a list

whenEmpty.description: Fallback: answer also without records, but only if no other http.response answers (e.g. 404)

maxRecords.description: Most records in the answer; more stop the pipeline, as they are held in memory

transforms.example:
status: 200
single: true
transforms.records: Passes all records on unchanged to all data links. Once its input has ended, it answers the waiting caller with them as a JSON list (with single, the first record), if it received any; with whenEmpty also without, as a fallback.
transforms.errors: Stops the pipeline when there are more records than maxRecords or the status is invalid. Without a waiting caller, or when the caller has been answered already, it sends nothing.
limits: maxRecords limits the records held in memory for the answer (default 10,000).

transforms.label: JSON Input
transforms.description: Reads the objects of a JSON or NDJSON file as records

path.description: JSON or NDJSON file to read, relative to the project folder or absolute

format.description: json: arrays and objects, also several one after another; ndjson: one object per line, a broken line goes to the error link; auto: ndjson for .ndjson and .jsonl, else json

records.description: Path to the array of records inside the document, with dots, e.g. data.items; empty: the document itself (json only)

encoding.description: Encoding of the file; auto recognizes UTF-8 and UTF-16 by their byte order mark and reads UTF-8 otherwise

fields.description: Fields to read, with path and type; empty: all keys of the objects as they are

from.description: Where the value is in the object, with dots for nested objects, e.g. address.city; empty: the key of the same name

type.description: Type of the value; empty: as in the file (numbers, text, true/false, lists and objects)

format.description: For values given as text: number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The value at from with the type of the field; without fields, every key with its value (whole numbers int, others decimal, objects and lists json)

transforms.records: Creates one record per object and passes it to all data links; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: A broken line of NDJSON goes to the error link with its text in the field line, a value that does not fit its type with the record; without one, the pipeline stops. Broken JSON, a missing records path and a key that appears twice in an object stop the pipeline.
limits: The file is read as a stream; a line of NDJSON may be at most 64 MiB.

transforms.label: JSON Output
transforms.description: Writes records to a JSON or NDJSON file and passes them on

path.description: JSON or NDJSON file to write, relative to the project folder or absolute

format.description: json: an array with one record per line; ndjson: one object per line; auto: ndjson for .ndjson and .jsonl, else json

ifExists.description: If the file exists: replace it once all records are written, or fail

fields.description: Fields to write, in this order; empty: all fields of the records

name.description: Name of the field to write

as.description: Key in the object, with dots for nested objects, e.g. address.city; empty: the name of the field

format.description: Writes the value as text with a number pattern like #.##0,00 or a date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy; empty: numbers as numbers, dates in ISO 8601

transforms.records: Passes every written record on unchanged to all data links.
transforms.errors: A record with a value that cannot be written (e.g. in its format) goes to the error link and is not written; without one, the pipeline stops. With ifExists: fail, an existing file stops the pipeline. The file is written to a temporary file first and replaces an existing one only once all records are written, so a failure leaves the old file.

transforms.label: XML Input
transforms.description: Reads the elements of an XML file as records

path.description: XML file to read, relative to the project folder or absolute; the encoding comes from the byte order mark or the declaration

records.description: Elements that are records: a path of element names with /, matched at the end of the path of an element (a leading / starts at the root); empty: the children of the root element

fields.description: Fields to read, with path and type; empty: attributes as @name and child elements as they are (text, objects, lists)

from.description: Where the value is in the record element: a child like amount, a path like customer/name, an attribute like @id or customer/@id, or #text for its own text; empty: the child named like the field

type.description: Type of the value; empty: as read (text, or objects and lists for elements with children)

format.description: Number pattern like #.##0,00 or date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy for the text; empty: 1234.5 and ISO dates

outputs.name: <fields[].name>
outputs.description: The value at from with the type of the field; without fields, attributes as @name, child elements as text, objects or lists, own text as #text

transforms.records: Creates one record per element that matches records and passes it to all data links; it has no incoming links.
transforms.errors: A record with a value that does not fit its type goes to the error link with its line; without one, the pipeline stops. Broken XML stops the pipeline with the line.
limits: The file is read as a stream; a record may be at most 16 MiB and nested at most 256 levels deep. External entities are not resolved.

transforms.label: XML Output
transforms.description: Writes records as elements of an XML file and passes them on

path.description: XML file to write (UTF-8), relative to the project folder or absolute

root.description: Name of the root element; empty: records

record.description: Name of the element of each record; empty: record

ifExists.description: If the file exists: replace it once all records are written, or fail

nulls.description: Empty values: skip writes no element, empty writes an empty one

fields.description: Fields to write, in this order, with where they go; empty: all fields of the records as child elements

name.description: Name of the field to write

as.description: Where the value goes in the record element: a child like amount, a path like customer/name, an attribute like @id or customer/@id, or #text; empty: a child named like the field

format.description: Writes the value with a number pattern like #.##0,00 or a date pattern like dd.MM.yyyy; empty: numbers like 1234.5, dates in ISO 8601

transforms.records: Passes every written record on unchanged to all data links.
transforms.errors: A record with an invalid element or attribute name, a control character or a doubled attribute goes to the error link and is not written; without one, the pipeline stops. With ifExists: fail, an existing file stops the pipeline. The file is written to a temporary file first and replaces an existing one only once all records are written, so a failure leaves the old file.

connectionTypes.label: FTP
connectionTypes.description: A server for file transfer over FTP without encryption; only with insecure: true

host.description: Name or address of the server

insecure.description: Required: FTP sends the password and all data unencrypted; set it only for a server without TLS in a trusted network. validate warns

timeout.description: Longest time to connect and sign in

connectionTypes.label: FTPS
connectionTypes.description: A server for file transfer over FTP with TLS

host.description: Name or address of the server

port.description: TCP port; empty: 21 with explicit, 990 with implicit

tls.description: How TLS starts: explicit (AUTH TLS on the usual port 21) or implicit (from the start, port 990)

serverName.description: Name in the certificate of the server if it differs from host, e.g. when host is an address

fingerprint.description: SHA256 fingerprint of the certificate of a server with its own (self-signed) certificate, e.g. AB:CD:…; several separated by spaces. With it Runnel accepts only this certificate; without it the certificate must be trusted by Windows

timeout.description: Longest time to connect and sign in

connectionTypes.label: HTTP API
connectionTypes.description: An HTTP API with its base address and sign-in, e.g. a REST API

baseUrl.description: Base address of the API; url of http.request is relative to it, e.g. orders?status=open

headers.description: Headers of every request, e.g. Accept; values may use ${secret:NAME}

auth.description: Sign-in: none, bearer (token), basic (user and password), apiKey (key in a header or the query) or oauth2 (client credentials)

apiKeyName.description: Name of the header or query parameter that carries the key

apiKeyIn.description: Where the key goes: header or query

tokenUrl.description: Token address of the provider (https://), e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token

clientId.description: Client ID of the registered application

clientSecret.description: Client secret of the application; use ${secret:NAME}

scope.description: Scope of the token, e.g. https://graph.microsoft.com/.default; empty: none

host.description: Name or address of the server

sslMode.description: TLS: verify-full (encrypted, certificate and name checked), verify-ca, require (encrypted, not checked) or disable

connectionTypes.label: SFTP
connectionTypes.description: A server for file transfer over SSH

host.description: Name or address of the server

hostKey.description: Fingerprint of the host key as ssh-keygen -l shows it, e.g. SHA256:…; several separated by spaces. Without it Runnel does not connect and names the fingerprint of the server to check

privateKey.description: Private key in PEM format (OpenSSH, PKCS#1 or PKCS#8), instead of or together with password; use ${secret:NAME}

passphrase.description: Passphrase of a protected privateKey; use ${secret:NAME}

timeout.description: Longest time to connect and sign in

connectionTypes.label: SMTP
connectionTypes.description: A mail server for sending mails

host.description: Name or address of the mail server

port.description: TCP port; empty: 587 with starttls, 465 with tls, 25 with none

tls.description: Encryption: starttls (port 587), tls (from the start, port 465) or none (only for a relay in a trusted network); the certificate is always checked

auth.description: Sign-in: password (user and password), oauth2 (an application registered in Microsoft Entra, e.g. for Office 365) or none (e.g. a relay that knows the sender by its address); empty: password if user is set

user.description: User name for the sign-in, often the mail address; with oauth2 the mailbox that sends

from.description: Sender of the mails if the action names none, e.g. Runnel <runnel@example.com>

timeout.description: Longest time to connect and send one mail, including the token request of oauth2

tenant.description: Tenant in Microsoft Entra (ID or domain, e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com); gives the token address

clientId.description: Application (client) ID of the registered application

clientSecret.description: Client secret of the application; use ${secret:NAME}

tokenUrl.description: Token address of another provider (https://); empty: that of the tenant at Microsoft

connectionTypes.label: SQLite
connectionTypes.description: A database in a single file, e.g. for local data and tests

path.description: Database file, relative to the project folder; created with its folder if it does not exist

readOnly.description: Open the database for reading only

connectionTypes.label: SQL Server
connectionTypes.description: A Microsoft SQL Server database, with a user or with the Windows account Runnel runs as

host.description: Name or address of the server

port.description: TCP port; empty: 1433, or the port of the instance

instance.description: Named instance, e.g. SQLEXPRESS (needs the SQL Server Browser service); instead of a port

user.description: SQL Server login; empty: the Windows account Runnel runs as (Windows only)

encrypt.description: Encryption of the connection: true, strict (TDS 8) or false (only the login)

trustServerCertificate.description: Accept any certificate of the server, e.g. a self-signed one; validate warns
